primer:
1 Build a sealed deck

  1. Sort. By colour, then mana value. Pull uncommons and up into their own row. Video
  2. Find the bombs and removal. These decide your colours more than anything else. Video
  3. Count playables per colour. You need about 23 good spells from two colours. The deepest pair usually beats the flashiest one.
  4. Check the signposts. Each pair has a gold uncommon and a hybrid uncommon built for it. Owning both is a strong pull. Video
  5. Pick a plan, not just two colours. Choose cards that work together toward one way to win. Video
  6. Fill the shape. 14 to 17 creatures, 4 or more two-drops, 3 or more removal, at most 3 cards at 6 mana and up.
  7. Lands. 17 lands, 23 spells. Split basics by how many cards of each colour you play.
  8. Splash only for power. A third colour is for 1 to 3 bombs or removal spells, with 3 or more sources: duals, planets, land searchers, Xenobotanist. Video

2 What wins sealed

  • Card quality beats synergy. Sealed pools are shallow, so games run longer and the best individual cards win.
  • Removal is gold. Your opponent opened rares too. Every clean answer you play is one of their bombs handled.
  • Flyers close games. Evasion ends board stalls, and sealed has many.
  • Two-for-ones add up. Creatures with enter abilities, beam me up spells and modal cards all give you extra value. Beam me up gives a spell a second cast. Video
  • Spacecraft are late threats. Count them as spells. They need creatures to station them. Video
  • Beam me up costs a creature, but that can help. Bouncing a creature with an enter ability lets you use that ability twice. Video

3 The 10 decks

WU Spacecraft

Play the best spacecraft, with enough real creatures to station them. Vigilance creatures attack, then station after combat.

Hemmer · Suurok-Class Science Vessel · U.S.S. Excelsior · Federation Field Medic

Modal spells and payoffs for choosing modes. Flexible: grind long or pull ahead early.

Seven of Nine · Resistance Is Futile · Consider the Prime Directive · Melkotian Adjudicator

BR Sacrifice

Lean and aggressive. Cards that make two bodies feed the sacrifice engines.

L'Rell · Tenacious Drone · Starfleet Security · Eject the Warp Core · Targ Wrangler

Extra land drops ramp into big creatures ahead of schedule.

Dal R'El · Final Frontier · David and Carol Marcus · Captain Michael Burnham

GW +1/+1 counters

Curve out wide and grow your team. Snowballs fast. The video's own deck.

Phlox · Emergency Medical Hologram · Dominion Supervisor · Dr. McCoy

Borg aggro: many cheap artifact creatures backed by efficient removal.

Locutus · Assembly Specialist · Command Subadjunct · Andromedan Automatons · Assault Drone

4 Bombs to build around

  • U.S.S. Enterprise-A, Free Spirit (white). Three 1/1s now, a 5/5 flying lifelinker next turn.
  • The Caretaker (blue). A 5/6 with ward that casts your opponent's cards for free.
  • Georgiou, Terran Emperor (black). You can't lose at zero life. Close to unbeatable unless they remove it.
  • Dominion Infiltration (red). Steals copies of their creatures for a turn. Scales with mana.
  • Captain Kathryn Janeway (green). Every creature explores, plus an extra land drop each turn.
  • Gowron, Eager for Battle (black-red). The best card for sacrifice.
  • The Inner Light (multicolour). Reanimates, draws, gains life and gives your team haste.

All from the video. Video

5 Playing to win

  • Mulligans. Keep 2 to 5 lands with plays in your first three turns. Mulligan 0, 1, 6 and 7 landers.
  • Play first. When you win the roll, going first is the default. Choose to draw only with a slow control deck.
  • Save removal for real threats. Kill what beats you: bombs, flyers, engines. Not the first 2/2.
  • Count their open mana. Before attacking into untapped mana, ask what trick it could be.
  • Station after combat. Station is sorcery speed. Attack first, then tap the creatures that stayed home or have vigilance.
  • Beam me up late. A second copy of a spell is worth more in a long game. Bounce a creature with an enter ability to use it again.
  • Race math. Each turn, count who wins the race. If you are ahead, attack. If behind, block and stall for your flyers or bombs.
  • Read the 8-power and Federation counters. Know when your payoffs turn on before you attack or block.

Between games

  • Matches are best of three. Your whole pool is your sideboard.
  • Sideboard for what you saw. Bring in artifact removal against Borg and spacecraft, reach or flyers against flying decks, and cheap creatures against fast aggro.
  • Switch colours if game 1 showed your deck can't win. A second build from the same pool is legal between games.

6 Drafting

Prerelease is sealed. Use this for Friday Night Magic or Arena drafts.

  • Pick order. Bomb, then premium removal, then evasive or high-value creatures, then good two-drops. Combat tricks and narrow cards come last.
  • Stay open for the first 5 picks. Take the best card, not your colour.
  • Read signals. A strong card of one colour at pick 6 to 9 means the players passing to you aren't in it. Move in.
  • Settle by pack 2. Two colours, one plan. Gold signposts tell you the plan. Video
  • Draft the shape. Track your creature count and two-drops as you go. Late picks fill gaps, not wish lists.
  • Draft is faster than sealed. Synergy decks like sacrifice, artifacts and counters are stronger in draft, where you can collect the pieces.

7 Common mistakes

  • Building around a cool rare in your thinnest colour.
  • Counting spacecraft as creatures, then having nothing to station them with. Video
  • Playing 41 or more cards, or 15 lands to fit one more spell.
  • Splashing a third colour for an average card.
  • Leaving removal in the sideboard for a creature that does nothing special.
  • Ignoring the uncommons. They show which deck your pool wants. Video
